column1: # Address layouts: id, country, language, kind, weight, template.
# kind `label` is a mailing label with one line per `\n`; kind `line` is a single line. A template is literal text and slots written
# `{slot}`, `{before|slot}` or `{before|slot|after}`; `before` and `after` are written only when the slot has content, and `before`
# is dropped when nothing precedes it on its line, so a missing ZIP or state removes its punctuation with it. A label line with no
# content is left out. Slots: recipient, organization, street, unit (a unit on its own line), city, state, zip, country.
# Layout sources: USPS Publication 28 sections 221 to 227 (a label's last line is the city, state and ZIP, no commas required) and
# the Canada Post Addressing Guidelines section 4 (city, province and postal code on one line, two spaces before the code; French
# addresses may put the province in parentheses). The single-line forms and the comma variants are how addresses are written in
